Ravi Kumar: Starting this thread to finalize the onboarding runbook items we promised to legal/sales: pin economics, migration windows, canary observability, and hardware-bucket notes. Keep replies short so I can fold into the doc.

Nora Diaz: Quick thoughts: separate pass/fail for gen vs embeddings. For gen use quality delta <= 1.5% and latency <= 1.25x pinned baseline. For embeddings use cosine drift < 0.5% and 99th percentile latency budget.

Becca (PM): Can we standardize names: 'pin' = model version hold, 'gracepath' = customer notice window, 'slow-migrate' = opt-in extended runway. That'll help comms.

Kenji Tanaka: Ops: we need a table mapping model families -> quant profiles -> hardware bucket (A100/H100) -> expected p95. I'll draft a CSV. Also include tokenization differences by family.

Ravi Kumar: Billing ask: should migration credits be percentage-based or fixed token allotments? Sales prefers percent (simple), finance prefers fixed (predictable).

Billing Bot: FYI: previous precedent: migration credits were flat token tiers in last enterprise agreement (tiered by monthly spend).

Becca (PM): Proposal to settle: default pin TTL = 30d. Enterprise opt-in 'gracepath' = 90d for a fee or token credit. Migration credit = flat token tiers mapped to monthly spend bands. That keeps billing simple.

Nora Diaz: Agree. Also: canary cadence = 2 weeks, start at 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> full, with daily quality checks and a hold if metric breach.

Kenji Tanaka: Canary signals we should monitor: p95 latency, error rate, tail token cost, model OOMs, and a sampled eval-quality delta. Instrument per-region and per-hardware-bucket.

Ravi Kumar: For gating, runbook rule: if any signal breaches threshold for 48h straight or spikes > 3x baseline, auto-roll back and open a Sev2.

Becca (PM): Comms plan: 30d notice for forced migration; customers on 90d gracepath get 60d notice and a migration calendar slot. We'll publish migration playbook with steps and rollback checklist.

Billing Bot: Suggested credit tiers: <$10k/mo = 15k tokens, $10-100k = 75k, >$100k = 300k. Adjust if finance objects.

Nora Diaz: Bench definition: canonical eval slice = stratified sample of 15k gen examples + 7k embed pairs, held-out for daily regressions. We'll version it (canonical_eval_v2) and keep provenance.

Kenji Tanaka: Hardware note: expect ~20% perf improvement H100 vs A100 for large families under FP16; 4-bit quant gives varied gains. Will add empirical numbers.

Becca (PM): Legal/sales templates needed: 1) Pin Addendum, 2) Gracepath opt-in clause, 3) Migration Credit schedule. Pradeep from sales to review.

Ravi Kumar: Action items: Nora -> canonical_eval spec + sampling SQL by Wed. Kenji -> perf table + hardware mapping CSV by Fri. Becca -> comms + templates draft by next Tue. Billing Bot -> confirm credit tiers with finance by Fri. I'll merge into a runbook PR after.

Infra Bot: Canary workspace created: model-catalog-canary-2222 on staging. Logs will stream to #eng-sre.

Nora Diaz: small note: we should include a 'customer rollback test' where we rehearse a migration rollback with one willing enterprise customer quarterly. Reduces surprise.

Becca (PM): Good idea. I'll add a quarterly rehearsal to the runbook and comms.

Ravi Kumar: Closing: thanks team. Expect runbook PR link in 48 hours. If anyone can't hit deadlines, reply now. :party_popper:

Kenji Tanaka: all good from infra side.

Billing Bot: queued finance review for credit tiers.
